prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create one production sprite atlas for Solar Friends, a warm painted Brazilian countryside village game. Reference image is STYLE ONLY, do not reproduce the houses. Transparent square canvas, SIX isolated sprites in a perfectly regular 3 columns x 2 rows grid with equal square cells. Each sprite wholly inside its cell with 12 percent transparent margins, no overlap, no text, no labels, no grid lines. Consistent 2:1 orthographic game projection, ground-plane slopes plus/minus 0.5, verticals upright, soft hand-painted materials and upper-left sunlight matching reference. Top-left: managed timber collection site, small stack of squared logs beside two small coppiced leafy trees and a sawbuck. Top-middle: a lush slender Brazilian bamboo clump with several cut bamboo poles resting beside it. Top-right: shallow ochre building-earth excavation with shovel, two earth-filled baskets, clear low earthen banks, no deep mine. Bottom-left: modest deposit of grey-beige stones with a short stack of selected foundation stones and a wheelbarrow. Bottom-middle: tidy rural salvage clearing, reclaimed teal door, cream window frame, small stack of terracotta roof tiles and reusable metal fittings, no garbage. Bottom-right: village receiving/workbench area, low timber pallet with a few crates, small blue solar panel leaning against crate, coiled pipe and simple camp workbench. Each object composition compact, comparable plot width. No people, roads, buildings, landscape background or cast shadow outside its footprint. Preserve genuine alpha transparency.
